paper.title: Doubly Optimal No-Regret Online Learning in Strongly Monotone Games with Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Single-agent bandit learning with smooth and strongly concave reward functions (bandit strongly concave optimization)
unmapped: rewards are maximised (concave) rather than losses minimised; strong concavity parameter beta corresponds to canonical alpha
settings.definition_quote: In our setting, an adversary first chooses a sequence of $\beta$-strongly concave reward functions $u^1, u^2, \ldots, u^T: \XCal \mapsto \br$ ... where $\XCal$ is a closed, convex and compact set. ... the feedback is limited to the value of reward function at the point that she has chosen, i.e., $u^t(x^t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-agent bandit learning in smooth and strongly monotone games (last-iterate convergence to Nash equilibrium)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in games with an equilibrium (last-iterate Nash convergence) objective.
unmapped: N-player (beta, lambda)-strongly monotone game; objective is E[sum_i ||x_i^T - x_i^*||^2] to the unique Nash equilibrium
players know beta and weights lambda_i
settings.definition_quote: A smooth and concave game $\GCal$ is called $(\beta, \{\lambda_i\}_{i \in \NCal})$-strongly monotone if we have $\sum_{i \in \NCal} \lambda_i\langle x'_i-x_i, v_i(x') - v_i(x)\rangle \leq -\beta\|x - x'\|^2$ for any $x, x' \in \XCal$.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-agent bandit learning in strongly monotone games with imperfect (noisy) bandit feedback
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in games with an equilibrium (last-iterate Nash convergence) objective.
unmapped: noise is a bounded martingale difference |xi| <= sigma
objective is E[sum_i ||x_i^T - x_i^*||^2] to the unique Nash equilibrium
settings.definition_quote: we replace Step 8 in Algorithm~\ref{Alg:MA} by $\hat{u}_i^t \leftarrow u_i(\hat{x}^t) + \xi_{i, t}$ ... (i) Zero-mean: $\EE[\xi_{i, t} \mid x^t] = 0$; and (ii) Boundedness: $\|\xi_{i, t}\| \leq \sigma$

conditions: reward functions smooth (gradient ell-Lipschitz), beta-strongly concave, Lipschitz
X closed, convex, compact with a nu-self-concordant barrier

source.label: Thm:regret-optimal
source.quote: Suppose that the adversary is limited to choosing smooth and $\beta$-strongly concave functions $u^1, u^2, \ldots, u^T: \XCal \mapsto \br$. Each function $u^t$ is Lipschitz continuous and satisfies that $|u^t(x)| \leq L$ for all $x \in \XCal$. If $T \geq 1$ is fixed and the player employs Algorithm~\ref{Alg:SA} with the stepsize choice of $\eta_t = \frac{1}{2nL\sqrt{T}}$, we have $\textnormal{Reg}_T = ... = \tilde{O}(n\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Paper's n is dimension d. Regret defined as max_x sum u^t(x) - E[sum u^t(x̂^t)] with deterministic oblivious functions, so equals expected regret. Proof bound hides nu, ell, L, beta, diameter; the d-dependence relies on nu = O(n).

conditions: smooth (beta, lambda)-strongly monotone game with unique Nash equilibrium x*

source.label: Thm:last-iterate-perfect
source.quote: Suppose that $x^\star \in \XCal$ is a unique Nash equilibrium of a smooth and $(\beta, \{\lambda_i\}_{i \in \NCal})$-strongly monotone game. Each function $u_i$ satisfies that $|u_i(x)| \leq L$ for all $x \in \XCal$. If $T \geq 1$ is fixed and each player employs Algorithm~\ref{Alg:MA} with the stepsize choice of $\eta_t = \tfrac{1}{2nL\sqrt{t}}$, we have $\EE[\sum_{i}\|\hat{x}_i^T - x_i^\star\|^2] = \tilde{O}(nT^{-1/2})$.

results.notes: Last-iterate squared distance to Nash; n = total dimension sum n_i. Step size does not depend on T, so recorded as anytime.

conditions: smooth (beta, lambda)-strongly monotone game with unique Nash equilibrium
noise is zero-mean bounded martingale difference with |xi| <= sigma

source.label: Thm:last-iterate-imperfect
source.quote: Suppose that $x^\star \in \XCal$ is a unique Nash equilibrium of a smooth and $(\beta, \{\lambda_i\}_{i \in \NCal})$-strongly monotone game. ... each player employs Algorithm~\ref{Alg:MA} with imperfect bandit feedback ... and the stepsize choice of $\eta_t = \tfrac{1}{2n(L+\sigma)\sqrt{t}}$, we have $\EE[\sum_{i}\|\hat{x}_i^T - x_i^\star\|^2] = \tilde{O}(\sqrt{\frac{n^2}{T}})$.

results.notes: Noise mapped to conditionally_subgaussian since bounded martingale difference.
